description: Every executable test suite in this repository, and what reaches it today. Reality, not intent: `trigger` says how a lane is actually reached and `owner` says who is accountable for it being green, so `unowned` with a written `note` is a permitted and expected claim. Discovery in tools/kd/src/runtime/lane-inventory.ts reads the repository's own state (workspace `test*` scripts, `kd test` subcommands, Vitest `exclude` globs, `*.e2e.test.ts` and `*.test.sh` files) and tools/kd/tests/lane-inventory.test.ts fails when a discovered suite is claimed by zero or more than one lane, or when a lane claims a suite that no longer exists. Claims are exact ids, never globs, so a new suite cannot be absorbed silently. `id` is permanent: verification records reference lanes indefinitely, so renaming one orphans its history. `triggerPaths` are repo-relative prefixes matched with `startsWith`, the per-lane generalization of the deleted .github/workflows/remote-e2e.yml `paths:` filter; an empty list means the lane is unscoped. This file is the single source of truth for them — `kd test remote-e2e --if-changed` reads the `remote-e2e-dev` lane here rather than a constant of its own. A prefix that matches nothing in the tree fails the inventory test. `hostCapabilities` is a closed capability set and never a machine id, because repo ids are machine-local and hosts come and go; `host` is the same requirement in prose, including conditions the vocabulary cannot express, and `hostCapabilities` is what a selector matches. `scope` declares which selectors should include a lane. Nothing reads it yet: the `kd verify` runner, the daily sweep and the ship gate are later increments, so a scope here wires nothing into any gate. This manifest records coverage; it does not cause anything to run.

lanes.description: The turbo fan-out over every workspace package's own `test` script: TS/Vue unit tests, offline CLI contracts, kd's own suite, and the narrow default slices of the headless-worker and linux-installed packages.
lanes.note: `.kanna/config.json`'s `test` array is exactly `["pnpm test"]`, which is what the merge singleton runs per branch. `tests/headless-worker#test` and `tests/linux-installed#test` each name a single file here; the real work in those packages is behind `test:gate` and is a separate, unowned lane.

lanes.description: The canonical broad local run: the workspace lane, the Bazel daemon build script, the Rust lane, then the desktop mock E2E lane, failing fast.
lanes.note: Composite. Nothing invokes it automatically: `.kanna/config.json` configures `pnpm test`, and no scheduler exists in the repository. It stops at the first red lane, so a failure in lane 1 says nothing about lanes 2-4.

lanes.description: Strict `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, then the workspace Rust tests with the daemon integration tests serialized behind the machine-wide Rust gate.
lanes.note: Reached through `./kd test all`, `.kanna/agents/ship/EXTEND.md`'s backport path, and operators typing it. Not in the per-branch checks.

lanes.description: The desktop mock E2E suite: the real macOS debug app driven through WebDriver against mock boundaries.
lanes.note: The Vitest exclude is why this lane never ran inside `pnpm test`; left out of every gate it rotted until a third of it was red, which is the precedent this manifest exists to prevent repeating. It is now the last lane of `./kd test all`.

lanes.description: The unattended desktop real E2E tier declared in apps/desktop/tests/e2e/realTiers.ts: real app to server to daemon/PTY, git worktrees, local/LAN/relay, Firebase emulators and companion-browser wiring.
lanes.note: docs/dev/testing.md states this tier runs "Nightly and pre-release". There is no scheduler anywhere in the repository — no launchd plist, no cron entry, no workflow — so nothing runs it on any cadence and nobody is accountable for its colour. The documented convention is not a mechanism. `test:e2e:all` runs every tier including the operator and Linux files and is claimed here because it has no separate trigger of its own.

lanes.description: The credentialed and provider-specific desktop real E2E files: deployed-cloud smoke, Codex SDK lifecycle, retained Claude-specific coverage.
lanes.host: macos with cloud credentials and provider accounts
lanes.note: Runs only when an operator intentionally supplies credentials; missing context skips files rather than failing, so a run of it can be almost entirely vacuous and still exit green. No standing owner.

lanes.description: The Linux desktop E2E files, which need a Linux desktop session real key events can be injected into.
lanes.note: Excluded from the default Vitest run on every platform and named by no gate or schedule. The Linux dev VM exists but nothing points this lane at it.

lanes.description: The full-bundle app update E2E: a real signed update bundle applied end to end.
lanes.note: Guards the updater path that ships to end users and is reached by no gate, no release step and no schedule.

lanes.description: The remote task interaction E2E lane against locally spawned kanna-server, daemon and relay processes: nine *.e2e.test.ts files covering terminal flow, task listing, LAN layers, secure channel, desktop peer channels and image attachments.
lanes.note: Standing red: terminal-flow alone measured 7 failed of 16 at 69239bc6b, reproduced in a control run, so this is lane debt rather than one branch's regression. `tests/remote-e2e/package.json`'s own `test` script enumerates six unit files and so excludes every file above from `pnpm test`, which is the same hiding mechanism that rotted the desktop mock lane. This lane's `triggerPaths` are the prefixes `kd test remote-e2e --if-changed` selects on, migrated here from the `REMOTE_E2E_TRIGGER_PATHS` constant so there is one copy; the flag works and is tested, but nothing invokes the verb automatically. Wiring it into the per-branch checks is deliberately sequenced after this red set is triaged, so it does not block an unrelated branch.

lanes.description: Staging health: the remote doctor followed by the staging remote E2E lane against deployed staging services.
lanes.note: Run by hand when staging is suspected to be broken. No schedule and no release step requires it, so staging drift is discovered by someone noticing.

lanes.description: Cloud sync E2E against the local Firebase emulator suite.
lanes.note: The one cloud lane that needs no deployed environment and no credential, and still nothing runs it.

lanes.description: Cloud sync E2E against deployed staging cloud services.
lanes.note: Requires KANNA_E2E_CLOUD_* credentials and refuses without them. No gate, schedule or release step invokes it.

lanes.description: Minimal cloud smoke against production cloud services.
lanes.note: Touches production, so it is correctly operator-gated — but no release or promotion step requires it either, so production cloud health is verified only when somebody decides to.

lanes.description: LAN sync between two physical Macs over SSH, with WebDriver tunnels and a cross-machine task visibility scenario.
lanes.host: two physical Macs on one LAN, reachable over SSH
lanes.note: Needs a hardware inventory file that is not committed. Unrunnable in the default environment and unowned; the manifest entry is the record of that, per the design's rule against writing another dated gap note.

lanes.description: The headless worker exit gate: create, execute, durable input, completion, stage fork and close, plus server restart and daemon replacement against real processes.
lanes.note: The package's default `test` script runs only src/providerPath.test.ts, so the gate files never enter `pnpm test`. kanna-worker is the Linux launcher and its supervision behaviour is verified by nothing on any cadence.

lanes.description: Install a built .deb with apt, run the worker under systemd --user, then upgrade to a second package with a live agent session and prove the session survived.
lanes.host: linux host where the test user can become root
lanes.note: Refuses to run off Linux, and the package's default `test` script runs only src/installedLayout.test.ts. `.github/workflows/linux-release-check.yml` runs installed.e2e.test.ts alone on hosted x86_64 and arm64 runners; the upgrade half needs two packages from distinct source revisions, which is wired nowhere. Under the directive to delete GitHub CI this lane has no replacement host yet.

lanes.description: Live agent CLI compatibility contracts: the real claude, codex, copilot and opencode binaries measured against the recorded fixtures Kanna's spawn paths depend on.
lanes.host: macos with installed and authenticated agent CLIs
lanes.note: The lane that would notice an agent CLI upgrading out from under Kanna — the drift that no commit in this repository can cause and no branch-scoped check can see. Everything skips rather than fails when a CLI is unavailable, so a green run proves less than it looks like. Nothing runs it on any cadence.

lanes.description: TUI fidelity: real terminal rendering compared against recorded frames.
lanes.note: Deliberately kept out of `pnpm test` as live and process-heavy, and then given no other trigger.

lanes.description: The terminal safe-region check inside the TUI fidelity package.
lanes.note: A second entry point in the same package, named by no documentation, no gate and no schedule.

lanes.description: The mobile Appium E2E suites on the iOS Simulator: smoke, cloud, relay, relay terminal control, hybrid, profile-disconnected, search focus, tab reselection, shell visual, and the preflight that checks the environment first.
lanes.host: macos with an iOS simulator and a running desktop server
lanes.note: Needs a simulator, an Appium server and the same machine's desktop server to pair against. Nothing runs any of them on a cadence, and mobile ships OTA, where a stale runtimeVersion is exactly the class of defect these would catch.

lanes.description: The physical-iPhone variants of the mobile Appium suites, plus the staging release-install check.
lanes.note: Correctly human-run — a physical device cannot be scheduled — but nobody is accountable for them being green, and a device can silently run a cached bundle, so a passing run here needs its own evidence that the branch's JS was served.

lanes.description: Appium server and XCUITest driver setup commands used by the mobile E2E lanes.
lanes.note: Not suites: harness setup that discovery surfaces because the scripts are named `test:*`. Declared here so they are accounted for rather than quietly filtered out of discovery, which would be a hole shaped exactly like the ones this manifest closes.

lanes.description: The App Review billing capture: a production-identity simulator build driven to the billing screens for App Store review evidence.
lanes.host: macos with a production-identity simulator build and an App Review account
lanes.note: Needs production credentials, so it is correctly operator-gated; it is also the evidence an App Store submission depends on and no release step requires it.

lanes.description: The mobile integration suites held behind explicit environment flags: agent provider inventory, Expo modules JSI worktree cache, and the Firebase account journey against emulators.
lanes.note: Each is gated on its own KANNA_RUN_* variable, so the files are inert inside `pnpm test` and the scripts are invoked by nothing.

lanes.description: The web portal's emulator-backed integration runs, including the account deletion journey.
lanes.note: Account deletion is an irreversible user-facing operation and its integration coverage is reached by no gate or schedule.

lanes.description: Shell fixture tests for the repo-config reader and the worktree setup script.
lanes.note: docs/dev/testing.md lists these under "run directly", which is the documentation's way of recording that nothing runs them.
